albums.blurb: Cobham was the drummer of the Mahavishnu Orchestra, and he cut Spectrum, his solo debut, in three days at Electric Lady Studios in May 1973 as that band was coming apart. Jan Hammer's Moog and the 22-year-old rock guitarist Tommy Bolin handle most of the soloing on the heavy side of the record, while Ron Carter, Joe Farrell and Ray Barretto appear on its jazzier interludes; the whole album is instrumental, and "Stratus" later became the backbone sample of Massive Attack's "Safe from Harm."
albums.reception: Spectrum reached No. 1 on Billboard's jazz albums chart and No. 26 on the Billboard 200, and AllMusic's Scott Yanow has retrospectively called it Cobham's best album.

albums.blurb: The Brooklyn band around singer-songwriter Samantha "Sammy Rae" Bowers formed in 2016 and spent nearly a decade as a touring act with only EPs to its name (The Good Life, Let's Throw a Party) before releasing this debut studio album on Nettwerk in September 2024: thirteen tracks of horn-driven, big-ensemble pop that pulls from funk, jazz and classic rock.
albums.reception: Its single "Thieves" reached No. 34 on Billboard's Adult Alternative Airplay chart, the band's first chart entry.

albums.blurb: The Pharcyde were four dancers-turned-MCs from South Central Los Angeles whose debut for Delicious Vinyl, produced almost entirely by J-Swift, offered a playful, self-deprecating, jazz-sampling counterpoint to the gangsta rap that dominated West Coast hip hop in 1992. The group never repeated its lineup or sound quite the same way again; the mellower follow-up Labcabincalifornia (1995) featured early production by J Dilla.
albums.reception: The album was certified gold by the RIAA in 1996, its single "Passin' Me By" topped Billboard's Hot Rap Singles chart and reached No. 52 on the Hot 100, and Rolling Stone placed it at No. 482 on its 2020 list of the 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.
